answers.learned: SQLBolt lessons 1–6. Joins are less mysterious than I had allowed myself to believe — I had been avoiding this out of habit, not difficulty.
answers.improve: Block the hours in the calendar rather than hoping for them.
answers.shipped: Nothing yet. That is the honest answer on day one.

answers.w-outcomes: None yet, but I found three initiatives from the last year where the numbers exist and simply were never written down. That is a week of work, not a year.
answers.w-evidence: Nothing public. SQLBolt finished, which is input rather than evidence.
answers.w-proof-gap: All of them, publicly. Analytics and Experimentation most acutely — those are the two the audit called must-fix.
answers.w-referrals: Zero. Deliberate — nothing to show yet.
answers.w-drop: Planned five days, did four. The plan was right; Thursday was not.

blockers: Evenings are less reliable than mornings

answers.learned: Wrote a window function without looking it up. ROW_NUMBER partitioned by user, ordered by timestamp — it finally reads as a sentence rather than a formula.
answers.blocked: Lost 20 minutes to a timezone boundary in a retention query. Worth losing.
answers.improve: Say the query plan out loud before typing it. It works, and it is also what the interview wants.
answers.shipped: First real dashboard from my own queries. Six charts, each with a "so what" underneath.

answers.m-artifact: Nothing published. Month 1 is inputs by design, but the pattern to watch is whether month 2 also ends with nothing published.
answers.m-skill: Analytics 6.5 → 7.1. Evidence: SQLBolt complete, Mode advanced module underway, one dashboard built from my own queries. Metrics 6.8 → 7.2 from three of the five frameworks.
answers.m-leverage: Mostly. SQL is the second-highest ROI item on the 80/20 list and it got the majority of the hours. The four-day gap mid-month cost roughly ten hours.
answers.m-stop: Nearly built a note-taking system instead of doing the work. Caught it. The audit warns about exactly this and it was uncomfortably accurate.

wins: Three of five KPI frameworks done
blockers: The four-day gap in week three
Nothing public yet — the must-fix items stay unfixed until something ships

prompts.question: What did I learn?
prompts.helper: One specific thing. "Worked on SQL" is not a thing learned.

prompts.question: What blocked me?
prompts.helper: Name the blocker precisely enough that it becomes actionable.

prompts.question: What should improve?
prompts.helper: One change for tomorrow, not a list of five.

prompts.question: What did I ship?
prompts.helper: Something that exists outside your own head.

prompts.question: What measurable business outcomes can I now demonstrate?
prompts.helper: From Part 10 of the audit. The answer should grow over 24 months.

prompts.question: What new evidence exists that I can operate at Senior PM level?
prompts.helper: Evidence, not effort. What could a stranger verify?

prompts.question: Which competency still lacks proof?
prompts.helper: Cross-check against the Skills page. Be honest.

prompts.question: How many referrals and recruiter conversations did I generate?
What feedback patterns emerged from interviews?
prompts.helper: Repetition is the signal. One-off criticism usually is not.

prompts.question: What did I plan and not do — and was the plan wrong, or the week?
prompts.helper: The distinction matters. One means replan; the other means protect the time.

prompts.question: What artefact did I publish this month?
prompts.helper: The monthly commitment. If nothing, say why without softening it.

prompts.question: Which competency score genuinely moved, and what is the evidence?
prompts.helper: Update the Skills page with the evidence, not just the number.

prompts.question: Did I spend my hours on the highest-leverage work?
prompts.helper: Compare against the 80/20 page. Effort in the wrong place still counts as zero.

prompts.question: What am I doing that the audit told me to stop doing?
prompts.helper: The stop list is on the Leverage page. Reread it.

prompts.question: Portfolio review: is this the strongest version of my portfolio?
prompts.helper: Quarterly checkpoint. Which artefact is now the weakest link?

prompts.question: Resume update: does every bullet carry a number?
Mock interview benchmark: what is my score trend by track?
prompts.helper: Quarterly checkpoint. Use the same rubric each time or the trend means nothing.

prompts.question: Networking and referral audit: who moved from cold to warm?
prompts.helper: Quarterly checkpoint. Relationship strength, not connection count.

prompts.question: Honestly: has my probability of a Tier-1 offer gone up this quarter?
prompts.helper: The audit's baseline is 65–75% over 24 months, conditional on execution.
